### 🎬 Story cutscenes
- A new survival world now opens with a cinematic intro. You come to on your back in the forest while a stranger, the Drifter, guns down two of the dead closing in on you with a KR-47.
- He brings you round by a fire. Then gunfire breaks out somewhere far off: his people are in trouble.
- Before he runs off towards the shooting, he leaves you a **map** and tells you to find him on your own.
- A few hours later you wake up alone, with the map in the grass beside you. The campfire is real and still burning, so you can use it.
- The scene is fully voiced, with subtitles, lip-synced dialogue and acted characters.
- In co-op, everyone in the world watches the intro together. Nobody can be hurt while it plays, and creatures leave you alone.
- Each story scene plays once per world and is saved with it.

### 🗺️ The map is in your hands
- Press the map key and you hold a paper map open in front of you with both hands. Put it away with the same key, or press any hotbar slot: the map goes down first, then the item comes up.
- The world map now looks like a printed survival map: green land, grey rock, blue lakes with a pale shoreline, yellow roads, buildings as white outlines. The fold lines and the torn edge stay.
- Settlements you find get a **name** lettered over their buildings ("Harlan Farm", "Depot Kilo-4", "Frostwell"). The name says what the place is and which biome it sits in.
- A new MAP card next to the backpack card in the HUD tells you which key opens it.

### 🛣️ Roads
- Settlements are now joined by dirt tracks. Follow a road out of a cabin and it takes you to the next place. Roads are graded into the ground, kept clear of trees and boulders, and show on the map.

### 🏘️ Towns
- The survival world now has **towns**: streets of houses, shops, a gas station and a church on flattened ground, roughly one every 2–3 km².
- Roads arrive in a town as its streets, and every building faces its street.
- Towns near you are on the map from the start, so you always have somewhere to head for.
- Buildings now show in the distance too, so you see a town on the horizon before you reach it.

### 🌲 A bigger world
- Biomes are now regions kilometres across (forest, desert, snow, burnt forest), not patches. Walk into one and you stay in it for a while.
- Ponds are fewer but bigger, from small pools up to 80 m lakes.

### 🧟 Buildings are never empty
- Every zombie spawn point inside a survival building now holds a zombie, day and night, from the moment you get near. A house is something to clear, not just a shell to loot.
- A house you cleared stays cleared for about three in-game days, and that survives a reload.

### 🫗 Canteen and campfire
- A canteen is now one flask with five sips. Fill it once at a pond, boil it once at the fire, and drink from it over a trip. The hotbar shows it as "3/5".
- Each raw sip carries a smaller sickness chance than a whole flask used to, but a whole flask drunk raw makes you ill more often than not. A full flask of boiled water fills the thirst bar.
- At the campfire, each click puts one piece on the fire and takes its materials out of your bag at once. Anything that ends the job early (death, taking it off, another recipe) returns the unfinished pieces to the fire's tray. The tray and what is on it are saved.
- The campfire and the cooking sizzle are now continuous recorded sounds instead of a crackle that restarted every couple of seconds.

### 🧰 Where do I get this?
- Hover any ingredient in the crafting book or at the fire and a card tells you what it is and where to find it: on the ground, off a bush, chopped from trees, broken from boulders, hunted, looted from zombies or mutants, salvaged from crates, made at a fire, or crafted on the mat.

### ⚡ Balance
- Taser: a hit now stuns for 3 s (was 10 s) and the shot recharges in 20 s.

### 🧟 Infection
- A new PvP mode: 15 seconds into the round one player turns into **Patient Zero**, and everyone a mutant kills turns too. Survivors win if anyone is still human when the clock runs out; mutants win when nobody is.
- Any survivor death infects you, a fall or your own grenade included. Players who join mid-round come in as mutants.
- The last survivor standing runs faster.
- Pick a 3, 5 or 8 minute round. It needs at least 3 players, and bots count.

### 🎒 Survivors
- Survivors gear up from the usual buy menu, with the same economy settings as the other modes, and can keep buying all round.
- Sentries and mines are off the menu in Infection.
- Dead mutants drop a little ammo for the gun that killed them.

### 🦑 Mutants
- Mutants are tall, fast tentacled creatures: 250 HP (500 for Patient Zero), running about 60 % faster than a survivor.
- In first person you see two tentacles that writhe and whip out at whatever you strike.
- Their tentacle lash kills a full-health survivor in exactly two hits, wherever it lands.
- Their **Q** is a fireball: it bursts on impact and leaves the ground burning, and it is good for flushing survivors out of cover.
- Bots play both sides.
